title: Prime Number of Set Bits in Binary Representation
summary: Given integers left and right, count how many numbers in the range [left, right] have a prime number of set bits in their binary representation.
statement: Given integers left and right, count how many numbers in the range [left, right] have a prime number of set bits in their binary representation. Recall that the number of set bits is the count of 1's in the binary form of a number.
constraints: Count integers whose number of one bits is prime.
hints: Within the input bound, popcount is at most twenty.
Precompute the small prime popcounts and count membership.
For each value, compute bit_count and add one when it belongs to the prime set.
Popcount exactly measures one bits, and explicit prime membership avoids repeated primality work.
editorial: Popcount exactly measures one bits, and explicit prime membership avoids repeated primality work.

tests.explanation: Six, seven, nine, and ten have prime popcounts, giving four.
Ten, eleven, twelve, thirteen, and fourteen qualify, giving five.
